**Reported titers**

| Compound | Titer | Strain / context | Where stated |
|---|---|---|---|
| Limonene | 14.12 g L⁻¹ (5‑L bioreactor) | Universal terpenoid platform built by site‑specific multicopy integration of MVA pathway + terpene synthase genes in HBQA7 (ref [16]) | p. 10–11 |
| (S)-Limonene | 22.8 g L⁻¹ (described as "highest reported"); Table entry 22,800 mg L⁻¹, fed‑batch, 100 h | HBQA7 → LSF6, via limonene synthase enzyme engineering and pathway optimization (ref [21]) | p. 9 (Table 2), p. 11 |
| Nerolidol | 32.33 g L⁻¹ (5‑L bioreactor) | Same multicopy-integration platform strain (ref [16]) | p. 10–11 |
| (E)-Nerolidol | 70.50 g L⁻¹; Table entry 70,500 mg L⁻¹, fed‑batch, 96 h | HBQA7 → LN62, nerolidol synthase engineering + competing‑pathway knockout (ref [24]) | p. 2 (abstract-adjacent intro), p. 9 (Table 2), p. 11 |

**Are they consistent?**

Yes — the two pairs of numbers are not contradictory, because they refer to different engineered strains and studies. The lower values (14.12 g L⁻¹ limonene, 32.33 g L⁻¹ nerolidol) come from the general-purpose terpenoid production platform of Wang et al. [16], while the higher values (22.8 and 70.50 g L⁻¹) come from subsequent, product‑specific optimizations (synthase engineering, fusion expression, competing‑pathway deletion) described in the following paragraphs (p. 11). The 70.50 g L⁻¹ nerolidol figure is also the value quoted in the Introduction (p. 2) and in Table 2 (p. 9), so it is used consistently throughout.

One minor formatting point: Table 2 (p. 9) lists only isoprenol (1410 mg L⁻¹) and isoprene (780 mg L⁻¹) for ref [16] and does not include the 14.12/32.33 g L⁻¹ bioreactor values mentioned in the text, so those platform figures appear only in the narrative on p. 10–11.
